cover.headline: A world-class contract manufacturer losing its biggest molecule: earnings have not found a floor
cover.lead: PI Industries makes patented agrochemicals for global innovators (76% of revenue), sells crop protection in India (19%) and is building a pharma business (4%). One customer, the owner of the herbicide pyroxasulfone, was **38% of FY26 revenue**, and that molecule is now going generic: the customer's purchases fell 28% in FY26, and on 11-Sep-2026 the originator, Kumiai, cut its full-year operating-profit forecast by 62% on falling generic prices. PI's revenue fell 16% in FY26 and 10% in Q1FY27, and management cut FY27 guidance to "lower single digit" growth. The street values PI on **P/E on FY28E earnings (30-34x)**. We forecast EPS of ₹68.0 in FY27E and ₹75.9 in FY28E, 9-15% below the street. Applying **26x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹81.6** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** The cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,269, DCF ₹1,305. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core molecule is going generic
arguments.p: PI's largest customer bought ₹3,540 cr in FY25 and ₹2,556 cr in FY26. Kumiai, the pyroxasulfone originator, brought shipments forward "ahead of the entry of generic versions ... into the U.S. market" (Jun-2026) and then wrote down inventory as generic prices fell (Sep-2026). New products are only 16-18% of CSM revenue, not enough to fill the gap yet.

FY25 was meant to grow ~15% and grew 4%; FY26 began with a "single digit growth" target and ended at −16%. In May-2026 management said FY27 would grow at "late-stage single digit or early-stage double digit at the worst case"; in August it said "lower single digit". Q1FY27 export volumes fell 8% and prices fell too.

arguments.h: New businesses cost money now, pay later
arguments.p: Pharma lost ₹149 cr at EBITDA in FY26 on ₹300 cr of revenue; global biologicals, electronic chemicals and PI's own molecules add more cost. Employee costs rose from 10% to 14% of revenue in FY26. Management targets pharma breakeven only at ₹500-600 cr of revenue, in two to three years.

arguments.h: Valuation: de-rated, but not cheap for falling earnings
arguments.p: At ₹2,310 the stock trades at 34.0x our FY27E and 30.4x FY28E EPS. Its 35x median forward P/E since 2021 came with ~31% a year EPS growth; we see FY29E EPS at about the FY26 level. Net cash (₹3,794 cr, ~11% of market value) cushions, but does not change, the call.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (early Nov-2026): whether exports start to recover as guided, and how far margins fell in the kharif quarter.
Pyroxasulfone: generic prices and volumes in the US, Australia and Argentina; Kumiai's FY10/2026 results (Dec-2026).
Registration and launch of Pioxaniliprole, PI's first own molecule (India, FY27), and partners for overseas markets.
Conversion of the US$1.2 bn CSM order book into H2FY27 revenue; the 4-5 molecules due to be commercialised in FY27.
Use of ₹3,800 cr of net cash: management is "evaluating inorganic opportunities".

sections.title: Three businesses: a global contract manufacturer, an Indian brand house and a pharma start-up

blocks.p: PI Industries, founded in Udaipur in 1946, has two old businesses and several new ones. Its **custom synthesis and manufacturing (CSM)** business, started in 1995, makes active ingredients and intermediates for global agrochemical innovators (Japanese, European and American) under long-term contracts: the customer owns the patent and the market, PI develops the process and makes the molecule. Its **domestic agri-brands** business sells crop-protection products to Indian farmers, many in-licensed from the same innovators. Since 2023 PI has added **pharma** contract research and manufacturing (PI Health Sciences), **global biologicals** (Plant Health Care, now PI AgSciences), **electronic chemicals**, and its own patented molecules.

sections.title: A long agchem downcycle, and generics eating the molecule PI depends on

blocks.p: Global crop protection is dominated by a few innovators: the eight largest (Syngenta, Bayer, BASF, Corteva, UPL, FMC, ADAMA, Sumitomo) sold ~US$56 bn in CY2024. The innovators discover molecules and increasingly outsource their manufacture to specialists in India and China. After the 2021-22 boom, the industry spent 2023-26 working off excess stock while Chinese generic makers cut prices. By mid-2026 the innovators were reporting flat sales: Syngenta's crop-protection sales rose 4% in H1 2026 (−1% at constant currency), with Latin America −11% on destocking. PI's MD called it the longest cycle he had seen, with only "early signs of demand and stabilization" in August 2026.

For a contract manufacturer the cycle matters less than the life of its molecules. A patented molecule earns well for its originator and its manufacturer until generics arrive; then prices fall and volumes shift to cheaper suppliers. That is now happening to **pyroxasulfone**: in June 2026 its originator Kumiai said it had brought shipments forward ahead of generic entry into the US, and in September it cut its full-year operating-profit forecast by 62.5% because generic entry outside Japan had pushed market prices down.

pair.source: PI Industries investor presentations, annual reports and earnings calls; GAM Research

pair.title: Export volumes: down for five quarters
pair.unit: Agchem export volume growth, year on year (%)

bullets: **The model.** PI develops a manufacturing process for an innovator's patented molecule, builds or adapts a plant, and supplies it for years. Customers rarely switch supplier during the patent life because changing a registered process is slow and costly. That gives PI sticky revenue and ~28% EBITDA margins in agchem; PI has never competed with its customers ("zero conflicts").

**The problem.** One customer took ₹2,556 cr in FY26 (38% of revenue; ₹2,336 cr shipped to the US), down from ₹3,540 cr. Analysts on PI's calls name the molecule as pyroxasulfone. Prabhudas Lilladher calls it "off patent"; Kumiai's own filings confirm generic entry in the US and elsewhere in 2026 and falling market prices. PI will not discuss it ("this is not our molecule, it is a partnership").

**New molecules.** 5 were commercialised in FY26 and 3 in Q1FY27, with 4-5 more planned for FY27. But products launched in the last three years were 15-18% of CSM revenue in FY25, 18% in FY26 and 16-18% in Q1FY27, so their rupee revenue has been flat to down, as an analyst pointed out in May. Management: adoption of new chemistry "has slowed down" in the downcycle.

**Order book and inventory.** The order book is "around US$1.2 bn", unchanged since May. Contract assets (product made for customers and recognised as revenue before dispatch) were ₹750 cr at Jun-2026, against ₹404 cr at Mar-2025; management says ₹500-700 cr is the normal range.
**Currency.** The rupee fell ~13% against the dollar over the year to Q1FY27, yet export revenue fell 12% on an 8% volume decline: PI shares currency gains with customers ("pass-through model").

bullets: **FY26 was hard:** revenue −7% (volume −1%) on erratic rain, lower crop prices, high channel stocks and a new licensing regime that froze biological sales for part of the year. Four products were launched (3 herbicides, 1 insecticide).

**Q1FY27 was better than peers:** volume +12%, revenue +3%, biologicals +50%. PI says it chose market share over price ("our approach has been to push and create market share"), while peers took price.

**Pioxaniliprole**, a diamide insecticide discovered in PI's own labs, is PI's first new chemical entity. It was filed for registration in India; management hoped for a launch within FY27 "depending on the regulatory framework" and plans filings in other countries over the next two years. It has not given a revenue target. Another new molecule (dicloromezotiaz, for diamondback moth) is planned for the coming season, which management expects to become a "three-digit" (₹100 cr+) product over 5-7 years.
**The 2026 monsoon** ended ~12.6% below normal (IMD, 30-Sep-2026). PI said in August that sowing had caught up with last year after a late start; the rabi season and channel stocks now matter more.

blocks.callout: Domestic is PI's steadiest business and the launch pad for its own molecules, but at ₹1,302 cr it is a fifth of revenue: even 10% growth adds only ~2% to group revenue. We model +4% in FY27 (deficient monsoon, pricing pressure) and +10% a year after.

blocks.p: PI has been building a second leg for five years. In the standalone accounts PI wrote down its investment in PI Health Sciences by ₹110 cr in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** PI's moat is **process chemistry and trust**: global innovators have given it complex molecules for 30 years, it handles hazardous chemistry at scale, and it has never competed with its customers. That moat protects PI *within* a molecule's patent life. It does not protect PI when the molecule itself goes generic, and today ~38% of revenue sits with one customer whose molecule is doing exactly that. The domestic business is a good brand house but not a moat; the new platforms have none yet. Net: a moat that is narrower than the 2021-24 valuation assumed.

sections.title: Five years of compounding, then two years of decline

blocks.p: PI's revenue grew from ₹3,366 cr in FY20 to ₹7,978 cr in FY25, about 19% a year, and net profit from ₹457 cr to a peak of ₹1,682 cr in FY24, as its export (CSM) business scaled up a handful of patented molecules for global agrochemical companies. Then growth stopped. Revenue was flat in FY25 (+4%) and fell 16% in FY26 to ₹6,714 cr as global customers cut orders and PI's largest molecule met generic competition. Net profit fell to ₹1,321 cr, and that includes a one-off ₹126 cr gain. Q1FY27 was weaker still: revenue −10%, profit −39%.

sections.title: More capital, less return: ROCE has halved since FY24

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 PI generated ₹6,678 cr of operating cash, spent ₹3,690 cr on plants and R&D assets, ₹989 cr on acquisitions (pharma in FY24, Plant Health Care in FY25) and ₹881 cr on dividends. It also raised ₹2,000 cr in a QIP (July 2020). Gross block went from ₹2,747 cr to ₹6,615 cr and capital work in progress to ₹1,030 cr. The returns have not followed: ROCE fell from 24% in FY24 to 15% in FY26, and ROE to 12%, because revenue fell while the new capacity, new businesses and a growing cash pile all sit in the denominator.

pair.title: Capex has risen as cash generation fell
ROCE: from 24% to 15% in two years

blocks.callout: **The test ahead:** management guides ₹700-800 cr of capex a year and says new plants take 4-5 years to ramp up. HSBC put it bluntly on the May-2026 call: ~₹2,600 cr of capex over three years and asset turns down from ~2.5x to ~1.5x. Capacity utilisation was ~80% in FY26. Until the new molecules fill the plants, returns stay low.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but watch working capital, one-offs and interest income

bullets: **One-offs.** FY26 net profit of ₹1,321 cr includes a ₹126 cr gain from writing back the Therachem earn-out after a settlement with the sellers (pharma), less a ₹23 cr Labour Code charge. Excluding them, profit fell ~26%. Screener shows the net ₹97 cr inside other income.

**Working capital.** Net working capital went from 73 to 139 days of sales in FY26 (annual report): receivables rose as PI gave "calibrated credit support" to Indian distributors, inventories rose, and contract assets rose to ₹698 cr. Cash from operations fell to ₹474 cr (₹1,413 cr in FY25), only 36% of net profit.

**Contract assets.** Under Ind AS 115 PI books revenue on some contract manufacturing as it produces, before shipment. That is allowed, but it means revenue can run ahead of dispatches; the balance went from ₹404 cr (Mar-25) to ~₹1,000 cr (Dec-25) and ₹750 cr (Jun-26).
**Interest income.** Other income was ₹316 cr before exceptional items in FY26, ~20% of pre-tax profit before one-offs. It depends on the cash pile and deposit rates, not on the business.

**Impairment.** The auditor's key audit matter in the standalone accounts is the carrying value of investments in subsidiaries: PI booked a ₹110 cr impairment on PI Health Sciences in FY26. Goodwill (incl. Isagro) is tested annually.
**Disclosure gaps.** PI does not disclose CSM vs domestic margins, the revenue of its largest molecule, or the losses of global biologicals and electronic chemicals.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit (Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP) is unqualified and the segment note reconciles. The amber is for the doubling of working-capital days, the reliance on contract-asset accounting, and the one-off gain inside FY26 profit.

sections.title: Net cash of ₹3,800 cr, but working capital doubled in FY26

blocks.p: PI has almost no debt (₹342 cr incl. leases at Mar-2026) and ₹3,542 cr of cash and investments, so it is net cash (₹3,794 cr on the company's count at Jun-2026, ~11% of its market value). The weak spot is working capital. Net working capital rose from 73 days of sales at Mar-2025 to 139 days at Mar-2026: inventories up, receivables up as PI extended credit to Indian distributors, and "contract assets" (inventory built for contract-manufacturing customers, recognised as revenue before shipment) up from ₹404 cr to ₹698 cr. Operating cash flow fell to ₹474 cr in FY26 from ₹1,413 cr. Q1FY27 released ₹300 cr (120 days), a good start.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for PI Industries (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven revenue on the three business lines the company discloses every quarter: Agchem exports (CSM), Domestic agri-brands and Pharma (PI Health Sciences). The company discloses EBITDA only for Agro Chemicals (CSM + domestic, incl. global biologicals) and Pharma, so CSM and domestic carry the same agro EBITDA margin. segments.name: Agchem exports (CSM)
segments._why: FY27: Q1 −12.7% (volume −8%, prices lower); management expects exports to recover in H2 on committed customer offtake and a US$1.2 bn order book, and guided total revenue growth to 'lower single digit' (Aug-2026, cut from high-single/low-double digit in May). We assume Q2 −8% and H2 +8-10% on a very low base: FY27 −2%. FY28 +5%: new molecules (16-18% of CSM, 3 commercialised in Q1) grow while the largest molecule, pyroxasulfone (now off-patent; its customer was 38% of FY26 revenue, down 28% in FY26), keeps shrinking. FY29 +8% as the new products scale.
segments._marginWhy: Agro Chemicals segment EBITDA margin was 28.8% in FY26 (AR note 35), but only ~26% in Q1FY27 (group 21.6%) on lower volumes, higher input costs and heavy spending on global biologicals, R&D (3-4% of revenue) and launches. CSM and domestic margins are not disclosed separately, so both carry the agro margin: 26.5% / 27% / 27.5%, below FY26.

segments.name: Domestic agri-brands
segments._why: FY27: Q1 +3% (volume +12%, prices lower; biologicals +50%). 5+ launches planned, including PI's first own molecule (Pioxaniliprole, awaiting registration on 30-Sep-2026), but the June-September 2026 monsoon ended ~13% below normal (IMD) and channel stocks are high: +4%. FY28-29 +10%: normal monsoons, the new molecule and biologicals.
segments._marginWhy: Same agro margin as CSM (not disclosed separately).

segments.name: Pharma (PI Health Sciences)
segments._why: FY26 ₹300 cr (+40%), but Q1FY27 −25% (order phasing). Management targets ₹500-600 cr of revenue 'in two to three years' to reach EBITDA breakeven (May-2026). We assume +10% in FY27 and +25% a year after, reaching ~₹515 cr in FY29: the lower end, a year later than the most hopeful reading.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA −₹149 cr in FY26 (−50% of revenue, AR note 35); Q1FY27 segment loss −₹82 cr before tax. Losses narrow as revenue scales: −45% / −25% / −10%.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Reconciling items: Screener EBITDA less the company's segment EBITDA (negative = adds to EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: FY26 EBITDA on Screener's basis (₹1,732 cr) is ~₹32 cr above the sum of the company's segment EBITDA (₹1,700 cr) because of how some items are classified. We carry ₹30 cr a year so forecasts stay on Screener's basis.
assumptions._capexWhy: Guidance ₹700-800 cr a year (May and Aug-2026 calls) across agchem plants (3 multi-purpose plants under construction), electronic chemicals, pharma (Lodi kilo-lab) and R&D. Q1FY27 ₹269 cr. FY26 actual ₹1,151 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹407 cr ≈ 6.6% of average gross block; Q1FY27 ₹104 cr (₹416 cr annualised) ≈ 6.2%.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and investments less borrowings (₹3,200 cr at Mar-26 on Screener; the company counts ₹3,427 cr of surplus cash net of debt, ₹3,794 cr at Jun-26). FY26 other income ₹311 cr before exceptional items on ₹3,847 cr opening = 8.1%; Q1FY27 ₹66 cr. Lower from FY28 as deposit rates fall.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹43 cr on Screener (company finance cost ₹16 cr plus lease and other charges); Q1FY27 ₹8 cr. Debt only ₹342 cr incl. leases.
assumptions._taxWhy: Management: ~24% for FY27 and after (22% in FY26) as more sales come from non-SEZ plants.
assumptions._payoutWhy: ₹15 a share for FY26 (₹5 interim + ₹10 final), 17% of EPS; 12-15% in earlier years.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash, but earnings swing with global agchem cycles and one customer: close to market sensitivity.

dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Replacement of maturing molecules with new ones keeps growth near global agchem plus share gains.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex runs at 10-17% of revenue today while new plants are built; ~6% in maturity.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values PI (Motilal Oswal 34x and Prabhudas Lilladher 30x FY28E EPS; HSBC quotes 28x FY28E). 26x = PI's 35x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021, cut by the 18.5% median de-rating of listed crop-protection peers by 30-Sep-2026 (~29x), and by ~10% more for growth: the 35x came with ~31% a year EPS growth (FY21-24); we forecast FY29E EPS at about the FY26 level. Bull 32x (its 25th-percentile multiple since 2021), bear 21x (its lowest since 2016).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts the ₹3,200-4,800 cr of net cash at face value instead of capitalising its interest at 26x. 16x Sep-28E EBITDA = PI's 26.6x five-year median trailing EV/EBITDA less the same de-rating and growth discount (~19.5x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~21% above the trailing figure.
